4b7a9dd3e1673eb3: SHAH ALAM: Police are investigating the disappearance of several residents from a private drug and alcohol rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, Klang, after its owner reported that a group of men and women had taken them away without the management's permission last week.
Klang Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the centre's owner on Oct 28.
He said the owner reported that a group of men and women had arrived at the premises and taken several residents away without the management's permission.
"The number of residents involved is still under investigation. We will provide updates as they become available.
"Investigations found that the rehabilitation centre is privately owned," he said in a statement last night.

a92e17a13e4166ef: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — How often have you driven far away for a particular dish or perhaps queued for a viral food item and emerged feeling disappointed?
All that time and effort spent for a mediocre, or even worse, unsatisfying meal. What sacrilege!

Psychologists call it effort justification, where people perceive a meal they had to work harder to get as special, better tasting, or worth the effort — whether it’s a long drive to Klang for bak kut teh or joining a snaking queue for many hours for the In-N-Out Burger pop-up or securing that elusive reservation at Khairul Aming’s Rembayung.
Perhaps a better approach to avoid this mind trap is considering whether a substitute is available nearer your home.
That possibility arose when I came across a review for Lala King Hong Bak/Klang Bak Kut Teh, a relatively new place in Taman Cheras.

Hong bak isn’t new; it’s what the Hokkiens love when they slowly cook pork, spare parts and chicken feet for many hours in soy sauce and a mix of herbs until the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender with a sticky, glossy sauce rich with gelatin.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Bak Kut Teh is brewed with 18 different kinds of herbs that give a deep flavour to the soup. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
You find it in Hokkien enclaves like Segambut and Klang but Jenjarom is hong bak central where a few places offer that meaty wonder.
This place in Taman Cheras was strangely quiet when I walked in, making me assume it must be a dud.
However, since I was there already, I decided to order a dish to try.
The moment my order for the Big Bone Hong Bak (RM19) hit the table and I smelled those strong herbal notes, saw the glossy sauce and that supple fat with the tear-apart meat... it was a done deal.
There’s a long list of other stewed pig parts, like the coveted pork trotter, curved feet, pig’s intestines, tendons and stomach.
According to a previous interview, the meat is marinated overnight with five-spice powder, pepper and light soy sauce.
After deep-frying, the meat is braised for over five hours in a broth brewed with eight different Chinese herbs, creating a thick, rich dark brown, fragrant sauce.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Sour & Spicy Hong Bak is an unusual version of the stewed pork belly with a hint of tanginess and distinct spiciness. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
The Sour & Spicy Hong Bak (RM19) intrigued me; it is reportedly a recipe the founder learned as an apprentice to an elderly couple in Klang.
One wonders what hardship he must have endured to learn this clever version of hong bak, where the tanginess and burning heat on the tongue alleviate the overly rich taste of the meaty brown sauce.
Eat the dish when it arrives at the table, billowing hot smoke from the claypot, as each piece of the pork belly is tender, yielding just slightly when you bite through the meat and fat.
It’s one of those dishes that can qualify for what Koreans call bap doduk, or “rice thief,” since the flavours are intensely savoury and require white rice to balance the strong taste.
There’s also Bak Kut Teh (RM19) featuring a dark, intense herbal broth that is fortifying; the meaty broth is said to be brewed with 18 kinds of medicinal herbs and roasted garlic.
Dig inside the claypot to discover enoki mushrooms, crisp iceberg lettuce softened in the broth, beancurd skin and thick sliced pork belly.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
La La Bak Kut Teh sounds like an unlikely combination but the two items work well to create a dish where sweetness tempers the strong herbal aroma. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi

Even when you say it out loud, La La Bak Kut Teh (RM25) is such an off-the-wall combination that seems unlikely to work but weirdly enough it does, as the sweetness of the shellfish tempers the strong herbal flavour of the broth, leaving you with a more refreshed palate as you fish for more of those thick white shells that cradle the plump molluscs.
La La Soup (RM25) is more conventional but done very well as the clams are cooked in a golden liquid perfumed with rice wine.
You’ll want to tip all that heavenly broth, complete with plump, juicy clams, into a separate bowl to finish.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
La La Soup is well prepared with just cooked clams and a rich broth laced with rice wine. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi
According to an old newspaper article I read, this place originally started in Seri Kembangan and created a buzz when it first opened.

Apparently, that location is closed, but they relocated to Kuchai Lama, where they operate out of an adjoining shop lot as a coffeeshop run by the founder while this Cheras location is managed by a related party.

I visited the two locations. Even though the Kuchai Lama location is supposedly run by the founder, the food felt off; their Sour & Spicy Hong Bak had an unpleasant sharp taste from excessive vinegar, making the dish difficult to finish.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The restaurant can be found on a busy street in Taman Cheras. — Picture by Lee Khang Yi

Not only is the cooking subpar, but the Kuchai Lama location is also staffed by foreign workers who cannot recommend dishes or answer basic questions about the food, making the Cheras restaurant the better, more consistent choice for dining.
Restoran Lala King Hong Bak/Klang Bak Kut Teh
14, Jalan KasKas 3,
Taman Cheras, Kuala Lumpur.
Open daily: 10am to 3pm, 4:30pm to 9pm

036a90bb52f8e9a8: MANCHESTER: The Bank of England (BoE) is expected to bow to inflation pressure from soaring energy costs and raise interest rates on Thursday, though it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year.

Economists polled by Reuters expect the BoE to raise Bank Rate to four per cent from 3.75 per cent, its first hike since August 2023, when inflation was still more than triple its two per cent target.

The BoE was criticised for underestimating how persistent inflation would prove the last time energy costs surged, and it is wary of being caught out again, with global energy prices high and little sign of a lasting end to the Iran war.
Back then, the BoE was among the first major central banks to raise rates. This time the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank have moved first.
BANK OF ENGLAND'S HAND "INCREASINGLY FORCED"
Governor Andrew Bailey has said the BoE cannot wait for conclusive proof of second-round effects, where higher inflation feeds into wage- and price-setting, or it will act too late.
But how much evidence is enough, and whether the drawn-out Iran war makes some second-round effects inevitable, have divided the Monetary Policy Committee, which voted 6-3 to hold rates in September.
Bailey said last month that businesses he had spoken to seemed to be absorbing higher costs more than in 2022.

In September the BoE warned that inflation would rise above four per cent early next year, and said the jump in energy prices since its July forecasts bore similarities to its "adverse" scenario, in which inflation risked becoming entrenched.
Inflation has since run hotter than the BoE expected. Consumer prices rose 3.5 per cent in the year to September, compared with the central bank's July forecast of three per cent.
"In other words, their hands are increasingly being forced, whether they like it or not," said Stefan Koopman, senior macro strategist at Rabobank.
"At some point, even a committee that would probably rather sit tight has to make good on at least some of what is priced (in the market). That time is now."
SOME MPC MEMBERS HAVE CRITICISED THE BOE
The Reuters poll pointed to a 7-2 vote in favour of a hike, with external members Alan Taylor and Swati Dhingra seen as most likely to continue to vote to keep rates steady.
Both have stressed spare capacity in the economy as a reason to wait, though recent growth figures have surprised to the upside.
Hawkish policymakers such as chief economist Huw Pill and external members Catherine Mann and Megan Greene have criticised the BoE's handling of the current episode.
But even they may baulk at endorsing market pricing of three to four more quarter-point hikes in 2027, which would take Bank Rate to between 4.75 per cent and five per cent.

"While we don't expect a clear steer from the Committee on how many hikes they're planning, it's possible that the meeting minutes or Bailey ... signal that Bank Rate is unlikely to reach the level that is priced in by financial markets," said Alexander Harvey, UK economist at consultancy Oxford Economics.
STATEMENTS WILL OFFER CLUES TO RATES OUTLOOK
Harvey said individual MPC members' statements would offer important clues to the outlook, particularly those of the BoE's internal members, whose views have been finely balanced.
Unlike financial markets, economists polled by Reuters last month were split on whether further hikes would follow after November's.

Mann has argued that aggressive bets on rate hikes reflect a risk premium the BoE itself exacerbated by adopting a "wait-and-see" stance after war broke out in the Middle East, rather than signalling clearly that it would keep inflation in check.
Alongside new economic forecasts, investors will be watching for the BoE's initial assessment of finance minister John Healey's budget, delivered last week.

Healey offered modest support to households and motorists struggling with higher energy costs, funded partly by a tax on banks. Economists said the measures would only slightly reduce the expected rise in inflation.
The BoE announces its decision at 1200 GMT on Thursday, with Bailey and some of his deputies holding a press conference at 1230 GMT.

1a92b203abe1b489: WASHINGTON, Nov 2 — Nine people were killed yesterday when the Learjet they were traveling in plummeted into a neighborhood in southern Florida, just miles from US President Donald Trump’s resort home of Mar-a-Lago, officials said.

Several unverified clips depicting the deadly crash and posted to social media show an aircraft nearly vertical slamming at high speed into the ground and triggering a large fireball, leaving a flaming crater near a busy roadside.
“Today’s plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida is a horrific tragedy,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement, confirming that all nine people on board were killed.
Duffy said the plane, a Learjet 60, had departed from Austin, Texas and was headed for the Bahamas.
The crash occurred near Cresthaven, a neighborhood in Palm Beach County that is less than seven miles (11 kilometres) from Mar-a-Lago.
Road closure after reports of a plane crashed onto the ground with some fatalities on November 1, 2026 in Greenacres, Florida. — Getty Images via AFP pic

Trump himself had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday and had departed from the nearby and newly renamed President Donald J Trump International Airport shortly after he boarded Air Force One at 11.55am, about an hour before the crash of the Learjet aircraft.
Storms had been reported in the area, and Trump carried an umbrella as he boarded Air Force One.
“The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate,” the crash, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement. — AFP
ad618abd4ab12829: PARIS: Lyon and Paris FC both won to close in on defending champions Paris Saint-Germain in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with the capital team defeating Monaco 3-1 despite a first goal of the season for United States star Folarin Balogun.
Lyon won 2-0 at home to Angers with goals in each half from Ernest Nuamah and captain Corentin Tolisso, as they bounced back from a 2-0 defeat away to PSG last time out.

The seven-time French title winners are third in the table, three points behind leaders PSG and one behind second-placed Lille. Lyon's win came amid reports that coach Paulo Fonseca is close to leaving the club to return to his native Portugal.

"I know that I will be with the players tomorrow morning but beyond that it is hard to say," Fonseca, who was in tears as he embraced his backroom staff at the end of the game, told reporters at a post-match press conference.
Fonseca, the former trainer of Porto, Shakhtar Donetsk, Roma and AC Milan among other clubs, is reportedly a target for Portuguese giants Sporting, whose own coach Rui Borges is under pressure.

Paris FC, who have big ambitions under the ownership of the mega-rich Arnault family, are fourth in the Ligue 1 table, behind Lyon on goal difference, after getting the better of Monaco at the Stade Jean-Bouin.
Lassine Sinayoko, the Malian international forward, scored twice late in the first half for Paris FC before Balogun pulled one back on 65 minutes.
- BALOGUN BACK BUT MONACO BEATEN -

Balogun is yet to start a game this season for Monaco after a turbulent summer featuring the controversy of his suspended red card while playing for the United States at the World Cup – after an intervention by US President Donald Trump – and then his refusal to sign for Everton on transfer deadline day.
He came on at half-time here and reduced the deficit with his first goal since netting in the USA's win over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the last 32 of the World Cup in early July.
However, Pablo Pagis soon scored a third for Paris FC, as Monaco slumped to a fourth straight Ligue 1 game without a win.

The match was a farewell for Paris FC's long-serving president Pierre Ferracci, who is now stepping down to make way for Antoine Arnault. He is the son of Bernard Arnault, the chairman of luxury goods conglomerate LVMH.
"A chapter is closing," said Ferracci. "I am delighted to have led the club this far and I am especially delighted about the great years that lie ahead."
Marseille beat Toulouse 2-0 in Sunday's late game with first-half strikes by Amine Harit and Amine Gouiri, the latter getting his sixth goal of the campaign.
OM have now followed a run of four straight Ligue 1 losses with four consecutive wins, and are up to sixth.

PSG are clear at the top of the table after a 5-1 victory at bottom side Le Havre on Friday, with Achraf Hakimi netting a hat-trick as Luis Enrique's team made it nine straight wins in all competitions.

Le Havre have not won this season and coach Didier Digard, a former PSG and Middlesbrough player, was sacked on Saturday by the club's American ownership, before president Jean-Michel Roussier resigned.
Lille beat northern rivals Lens 1-0 on Friday with a late goal from 40-year-old Olivier Giroud.

Strasbourg beat Auxerre 5-1 in Sunday's early game, ending a run of four straight defeats, as Moroccan international Gessime Yassine set up one goal, won a penalty, and then scored twice himself late on.
English forward Cameron Archer got Auxerre's goal and now has six in seven Ligue 1 appearances on loan from Southampton.--AFP

806483d326347c00: MADRID, (Spain): Four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed in last week's high-speed train collision in Spain, authorities said.

Wednesday's disaster — one of Europe's deadliest rail accidents this century — has seen victims' relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts.
A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Sunday the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims.
It had already announced the deaths of a French and a Portuguese citizen, as well as that of 54 Spaniards.
All but three of the victims are now identified, the statement added.
Three reports for missing people remain active, the authorities said. They concern two Australians and one Japanese citizen.
"As the contacted families have expressed their wish to travel to Spain to carry out in-person identification, we are awaiting their arrival in the country," the statement said.

The accident was Spain's second high-speed train collision this year and raised fresh questions about the country's rail safety, after a crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people.

The latest disaster struck when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to Spanish company Iryo outside the central village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid.

The failure of an automatic safety system halted all trains on a 63-kilometre stretch of track, but a control centre authorised the Renfe service to resume its journey while the other train was still.
The tragedy came one month before a November 29 general election in which Socialist leader Pedro Sanchez will seek to overcome unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership. — AFP

Mann, 83, is said to be an experienced target shooter and is known for the intense and realistic gunplay in his movies, many of which are staples of the crime thriller genre.
He has directed an array of well-known films, including "Thief," "The Last of the Mohicans," "Public Enemies," "The Insider" and "Ali."
But he is perhaps best known for "Heat," which pitted Robert De Niro playing a master criminal against Al Pacino's police officer in a taut thriller.
The film's iconic final scene sees Pacino stalking De Niro in the dark beside an airport runway, both men with their guns drawn.--AFP

cea7f2c9bb3f929a: SARAWAK presents Malaysia with a revealing economic question. How can a state rank among the country's strongest producers of economic value while its typical household receives less income than the national median?
The Statistics Department revised 2024 figures bring the question into focus. Sarawak logged gross domestic product (GDP) per capita of RM73,253, above the national figure of RM56,772.
Yet its median gross monthly household income was RM5,504, compared with Malaysia's RM7,017. Its mean household income, RM6,947, was also below the national average of RM9,155.
Using 2024 provides a common reference year for production and household income. The figures describe different aspects of prosperity.
Their divergence deserves a careful explanation and should inform how development is assessed.
TWO MEASURES OF PROSPERITY
GDP measures the value added by production within a territory. GDP per capita divides that annual value by the population.
It is neither an average salary nor the amount available for each resident to spend.
Household income records receipts from employment, self-employment, property and investment, and transfers.
The median identifies the household in the middle of the income distribution. The department's household survey covers Malaysian citizen households, while GDP has a broader production coverage.
These measures therefore have different units and coverage.
Subtracting monthly household income from annual GDP per capita would produce no meaningful estimate of wealth lost or income retained.
The useful comparison concerns their positions against the corresponding national benchmarks.
Sarawak's oil and gas, liquefied natural gas and energy-intensive industries help explain its substantial production base.

Such activities require considerable capital and can generate high value with relatively few workers. Their productivity need not be reflected in the earnings of people employed elsewhere in the economy.
Ownership matters. Income generated within a state can accrue to companies, investors or workers resident elsewhere.
Corporate earnings may be retained for investment or distributed to shareholders. Tax revenues may finance services across the federation.
The geography of production consequently differs from the geography of income received. The size of these flows must be established through evidence.
The headline figures alone cannot tell us which mechanism contributes most to Sarawak's household income position.
FOLLOW THE INCOME
A more useful inquiry begins with the industries. How much income do they generate for resident workers? What business do they create for local firms? How do those firms improve productivity and pay?
Consider two industrial projects of comparable size. One might procure most specialist services externally and offer limited opportunities for local suppliers.
Another might develop engineering companies, train technicians and establish sustained ties relationships with nearby firmsenterprises.
Their investment announcements could look similar, while their wider economic consequences differ substantially.
This is an illustration of what should be investigated. Establishing the pattern in Sarawak requires procurement, employment and ownership evidence.
A supplier's registered address alone would reveal little about where its work is performed or how much value it adds locally.
The accounting must be precise. Imported intermediate inputs are excluded when domestic value added is calculated. They should not then be deducted from GDP a second time.
Imported machinery and expertise can improve productivity and create opportunities. Purchases from other states can support a more competitive Sarawak industry.
Successful integration should boost increase Sarawak's ability to earn income through national and international supply chains.
Keeping every ringgit within state boundaries would be an unsuitable objective.
Households benefit through public services. Resource-related revenues can support education, healthcare and infrastructure even when those benefits do not appear as cash income in a household survey.
Any assessment of prosperity must consider this wider contribution, alongside the costs families face and the quality of services they receive.
MEASURE WHAT FAMILIES GAIN
The policy implication is to examine the connection between productive industries and the people living around them.
More investment can expand opportunities, but its contribution to household prosperity depends on the jobs, supplier ties and public benefits it creates.
Regional input-output accounts could help map purchases between industries and across state boundaries.
Linking these accounts to labour-market, ownership and household data through a regional social accounting matrix would provide a fuller picture of how income reaches different groups.
An ordinary input-output table cannot identify every household beneficiary or the ultimate recipients of company dividends.
A useful assessment would track resident earnings, access to skilled work and the value added by local suppliers.
It should distinguish developments in industrial centres from conditions in more remote communities. State averages can conceal differences that require different policy responses.
Public reporting should distinguish projected benefits from realised outcomes.

Investment approvals and modelled multipliers provide useful information, but families experience actual wages, dependable services and opportunities that they can reach. Those outcomes deserve equal prominence in the development account.

This would make the debate more constructive. It would help governments identify where infrastructure is still the binding constraint, where skills are scarce and where firms need support to meet industrial requirements. It would also allow successful programmes to be recognised on evidence.
Sarawak's productive strength gives it substantial opportunities. The next task is to show how effectively that strength improves the economic lives of its people.
A state's prosperity acquires its fullest meaning when households can see the gains in their earnings, security and opportunities.

*Economist Samirul Ariff Othman is an international relations analyst and a senior consultant with Global Asia Consulting (GAC). Samirul has a background as a senior researcher at the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research. The viewpoints articulated are solely those of the author.

80dc5d4bcd8af497: The rumour mill is back spinning with the story of a merger between Maxis Bhd and U Mobile Sdn Bhd.

While the recent report by a foreign wire service on the possibility of a merger between Maxis and U Mobile is not the first time such a story had come up, it still attracts market attention due to the impact it could have on the country's telecom sector.

A merged Maxis-U Mobile entity would overtake CelcomDigi Bhd as the country's largest mobile operator by subscribers. As of Oct 30, Maxis is valued at RM27.9 billion, while CelcomDigi is about RM1 billion bigger in market value.

After the story broke last Wednesday (Oct 28), Maxis' shareholders reacted negatively to the story, with its share price falling 3.8 per cent to close at RM3.51. The stock fell 5.2 per cent during trading hours that day, the biggest intraday decline since June.

The negative reaction to the story could be due to the dilutive impact that such a merger would have on Maxis' shares, depending on the valuation of U Mobile agreed by both companies. The higher the valuation, the more dilution to Maxis' share value.
What is the value of U Mobile for Maxis, if indeed the companies are courting each other?

In a statement to Business Times' queries, Maxis said it is always evaluating strategic opportunities and partnerships that are value accretive. A merger with U Mobile can be value accretive to Maxis, in the long run, due to the second 5G network.
U Mobile operates Malaysia's second 5G network alongside Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB). The asset that U Mobile has – 100MHz block within the 3.5Ghz and 3.6GHz band – is what makes it valuable.

Malaysia's 5G network operates on a dual network model. DNB, which was supposed to be the country's sole operator until the change in policy in 2024, operates the network on two 100MHz blocks between the 3.3GHz and 3.4GHz, and 3.4GHz and 3.5GHz bands.

Currently, Maxis, CelcomDigi and YTL Communications Sdn Bhd are on DNB's network. The three are also equal shareholders of DNB, after the Minister of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) exercised its put option requiring them to acquire its shares on Dec 1, 2025.
U Mobile had exited DNB on June 30, following its appointment as the second 5G network operator.

However, developing the 5G network is not cheap. According to a telco executive, one 5G site costs around RM200,000 to be developed, excluding equipment. DNB had set up 7,489 sites in developing the network.

"The cost of investment in the 5G network might not be justified, if not shared across operators, as average revenue per users (ARPU) has been declining over the past few years," says the telco executive Business Times spoke to.
In the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, Maxis' postpaid ARPU declined 1.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to RM70.50 per month, while CelcomDigi's fell 4.5 per cent QoQ to RM60.

"Customers are not willing to pay more for data. If a mobile network operator (MNO) wants to invest in a network, it will need to grow its customer base tremendously, which is perhaps the reason for the Maxis-U Mobile merger to come up again," the executive says.

When DNB was rolled out as the country's sole 5G network operator, the cost was touted at RM16.5 billion over 10 years. Recently, DNB raised a RM5.2 billion Islamic syndicated financing to refinance its government guarantee revolving credit, as well as for further investments.

A look at U Mobile's financials with the Companies Commission of Malaysia reveals that the company has an accumulated loss of RM6.3 billion as of Dec 31, 2025, with a net loss of RM1.6 billion during the year.
This shows that while U Mobile has been growing its subscribers, it has yet to translate into profitability.
MERGER MUST GET CELCOMDIGI, YTL POWER'S AGREEMENTS
A merger between Maxis and U Mobile also depends on whether Maxis could get out of DNB. This is because a telco is not allowed to have ownerships in both 5G networks.

Currently, Maxis, CelcomDigi and YTL Power International Bhd each own 33.33 per cent of DNB. If Maxis were to merge with U Mobile, it would have to sell its stake to either CelcomDigi or YTL Power, or both.

Considering that each company already holding 33.33 per cent stake, a sale of Maxis' stake would mean DNB will be a subsidiary of both CelcomDigi and YTL Power. Whether this is something palatable for either is a question.
As of the financial year ended Dec 31, 2024, DNB recorded a net loss of RM1.2 billion, and accumulated loss of RM3.16 billion. The network operator is expected to remain loss-making until 2030.

Throughout the years, the shareholding structure of DNB has been changed twice. The first happened in June 2024, when CelcomDigi, Maxis, U Mobile and YTL Power collectively acquired 65.1 per cent stake, giving each an interest of approximately 16.3 per cent.

When U Mobile became the second network operator, it disposed of its 100,000 DNB shares to CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL, giving the remaining shareholders 19.44 per cent each. Then their shareholdings increased to 33.33 per cent following the put option exercised by MoF Inc.
The put option requires each of the remaining shareholders to fork out RM327.87 million to MoF Inc.
While the exercise is not yet completed, the exit of the government-owned company also means that the private investors now have to hold the risks of developing the 5G network themselves.

The transfer of ownership is expected to be completed by the end of this year. This means that DNB associate contributions will begin appearing in Maxis, CelcomDigi, and YTL Power's financial statements from the fourth quarter of 2026.
The full impact of DNB's contributions to profit and loss will be felt in 2027.
Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) in a research note on Oct 29 stated that it had flagged a Maxis – U Mobile merger as a live risk weighing on both Maxis and CelcomDigi.
"If the merger materialises, we believe the near-term implications would be negative given higher capex for 5G, weaker earnings, and dividend pressures for both Maxis and CelcomDigi.

"But, beyond that, the prospect of a market repair in a two-player market is strong because the aggressive price competitor (i.e. U Mobile) is being absorbed, which should reinforce pricing discipline in the market," said HLIB.

A merger between Maxis and U Mobile would create a more meaningful two-player market, as the combined entity would have a subscriber base that is broadly on par with CelcomDigi. On top of that, Telekom Malaysia Bhd is also on the second network.
But it will also put pressure on CelcomDigi and YTL Power to shoulder the cost of developing DNB's network. Will they then, if the merger were to happen, acquire Maxis' shares in DNB?

c9a70f117e0dc251: PETALING JAYA: New political configurations have reshaped the political landscape in Melaka, making the narrow margins witnessed in the 2021 state election a poor benchmark to predict the outcome of the coming polls.

Thirteen seats, most of them Malay-majority strongholds, were won with majorities of under 1,000 votes in 2021 as Barisan Nasional, Perikatan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan clashed in all 28 constituencies.
But it will be different this time, although there are 17 multi-cornered fights in the Nov 14 polls, says political analyst Hisomuddin Bakar of Ilham Centre.
With BN and PN having formed an alliance, a unified Malay vote could turn the formerly slim wins into comfortable victories for the Malay unity pact, even in mixed seats.
Additionally, the bulk of the 17 multi-cornered battles on Nov 14 involve Bersama, a PKR splinter launched just this year.

"The BN-PN cooperation will give a structural advantage in the 21 seats BN won in 2021. The unifying of these two political forces, who used to be rivals, could produce an organised consolidation of Malay votes.
"The results of the 2021 Melaka state election, particularly seats won by narrow margins, can no longer be used as an absolute benchmark for assessing the contest this time," he told FMT.

Nonetheless, the analyst said the BN-PN alliance may not necessarily result in a transfer of votes for all coalition component parties, especially PN's Wawasan, primarily composed of former Umno leaders such as Hamzah Zainudin, Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, Ronald Kiandee and Abdul Rahim Thamby Chik, among many others.

The defection of these leaders from Umno to Bersatu following BN's fall from power in 2018 was still a sore point for Umno's grassroots, potentially deterring them from backing Wawasan candidates, said Hisomuddin.
"An agreement at the leadership level does not necessarily translate into a smooth transfer of votes among voters," he added.
Wawasan is contesting the mixed seat of Bemban, won by Bersatu in 2021, and the DAP stronghold of Kesidang.
BN is contesting 23 seats while PN vies for the remaining five under their alliance.
PH, which has fielded 24 candidates, has formed a similar pact with former component Bersatu, which is contesting seven seats. They will clash in three constituencies.
2 other major changes

Hisomuddin said there were two other major differences with the 2021 election - the Melaka electorate has grown from 495,195 to 687,697 voters, and the country has recovered from the Covid-19 pandemic, which accounted for the low turnout in 2021.
The election then was also held just a month before the voting age was reduced to 18 and automatic voter registration took effect.
Hisomuddin said young voters will be a key segment for all parties; these voters were more dynamic, unpredictable and did not hold political allegiances unlike traditional voters.
"Their support is heavily influenced by current trends, their perception of candidates, issues that hit close to home and the effectiveness of campaign communications.

"Therefore, any party still has a chance at staging a surprise if they field the right candidate, present an attractive campaign message, and employs an aproach that truly understands the aspirations of young voters," he said.
More challengers in marginal seats
Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia said the multi-cornered battles involved more marginal seats from 2021, and the outcome could be determined by how the votes would be split.
Parties with a poor track record could face defeats, while the new political alliances could shut out even those assemblymen with a track record, especially in non-BN seats.
"These constituencies have many undecided voters. Some may only decide at the last minute, depending on current issues, political messaging or public sentiment," he said.
6dfb652209bcfc8c: PETALING JAYA: Pembentukan pakatan politik baharu pada PRN Melaka mengubah landskap persaingan sehingga keputusan tipis lima tahun lalu tidak lagi sesuai dijadikan ukuran utama untuk menjangka keputusan kali ini.

Pada PRN 2021, sebanyak 13 kerusi, kebanyakannya kawasan majoriti Melayu, dimenangi dengan majoriti kurang 1,000 undi ketika Barisan Nasional (BN), Perikatan Nasional (PN) dan Pakatan Harapan (PH) bertembung di semua 28 DUN.
Namun, Hisomuddin Bakar daripada Ilham Centre berkata keadaan kali ini berbeza walaupun PRN 14 Nov menyaksikan 17 pertandingan pelbagai penjuru.

Katanya, kerjasama BN dan PN berpotensi menyatukan sebahagian besar undi Melayu yang sebelum ini berpecah antara kedua-dua gabungan, sekali gus memberi kelebihan kepada pakatan itu termasuk di kerusi campuran.
Selain itu, kebanyakan pertandingan pelbagai penjuru kali ini membabitkan Bersama, parti serpihan PKR yang ditubuhkan tahun ini.

“Kerjasama BN-PN memberi kelebihan dari segi struktur di 21 kerusi yang dimenangi BN pada 2021. Penyatuan dua kekuatan politik yang sebelum ini bersaing boleh membawa kepada penggabungan undi Melayu secara lebih tersusun.
“Keputusan PRN Melaka 2021, khususnya di kerusi yang dimenangi dengan majoriti tipis, tidak lagi boleh dijadikan ukuran mutlak untuk menilai persaingan kali ini,” katanya kepada FMT.

Bagaimanapun, Hisomuddin berkata kerjasama BN-PN tidak semestinya menjamin pemindahan undi antara penyokong semua parti komponennya, khususnya kepada Wawasan yang dianggotai ramai bekas pemimpin Umno.
Antara pemimpin Wawasan ialah Hamzah Zainudin, Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, Ronald Kiandee dan Abdul Rahim Thamby Chik.

Menurutnya, tindakan beberapa pemimpin itu meninggalkan Umno untuk menyertai Bersatu selepas BN kehilangan kuasa pada 2018 masih menjadi isu dalam kalangan akar umbi Umno dan mungkin menyebabkan sebahagian mereka sukar menerima calon Wawasan.
“Persetujuan di peringkat kepimpinan tidak semestinya bermakna undi penyokong dapat dipindahkan dengan lancar,” katanya.
Wawasan bertanding di Bemban, kerusi campuran yang dimenangi Bersatu pada 2021, selain kubu kuat DAP di Kesidang.
BN bertanding di 23 kerusi manakala PN di lima kerusi menerusi kerjasama mereka pada PRN kali ini.
PH pula meletakkan 24 calon dan membentuk kerjasama dengan Bersatu, yang bertanding di tujuh kerusi, dengan kedua-duanya bertembung di tiga kawasan.
Dua perubahan besar

Hisomuddin berkata, terdapat dua lagi perubahan penting berbanding PRN 2021, iaitu jumlah pengundi Melaka meningkat daripada 495,195 kepada 687,697 orang dan negara kini sudah pulih daripada pandemik Covid-19 yang antara faktor menyebabkan peratusan keluar mengundi rendah ketika itu.
PRN 2021 juga berlangsung hanya kira-kira sebulan sebelum umur mengundi diturunkan kepada 18 tahun dan pendaftaran pemilih automatik dilaksanakan.
Menurutnya, pengundi muda akan menjadi kelompok penting bagi semua parti kerana mereka lebih dinamik, sukar dijangka dan tidak mempunyai kesetiaan politik sekuat pengundi tradisional.
“Sokongan mereka banyak dipengaruhi trend semasa, pandangan terhadap calon, isu yang dekat dengan kehidupan mereka serta keberkesanan komunikasi kempen.

“Justeru, mana-mana parti masih mempunyai peluang mencipta kejutan jika mengetengahkan calon sesuai, membawa mesej kempen yang menarik dan menggunakan pendekatan yang benar-benar memahami aspirasi pengundi muda,” katanya.
Lebih ramai pencabar di kerusi marginal

Sementara itu, Mazlan Ali daripada Universiti Teknologi Malaysia berkata banyak pertandingan pelbagai penjuru kali ini berlaku di kerusi yang mencatat keputusan tipis pada 2021, menyebabkan pecahan undi menjadi faktor penting.

Katanya, parti yang mempunyai rekod prestasi kurang baik berisiko tewas, manakala pakatan politik baharu juga boleh menjejaskan penyandang walaupun mempunyai rekod perkhidmatan, khususnya di kerusi bukan milik BN.

“Kerusi seperti ini mempunyai ramai pengundi belum membuat keputusan. Ada yang mungkin hanya menentukan pilihan pada saat akhir bergantung kepada isu semasa, mesej politik atau sentimen orang ramai,” katanya.
6df37f80199c7b44: KUALA LUMPUR: Matcha has travelled a long way from the tea bowl. The finely powdered Japanese green tea first became a café staple in lattes and desserts, then spread to roadside drinks and baked goods.
Now, its unmistakable green colour is turning up in far less predictable places: nasi lemak, burgers, noodles, and even ayam gepuk and fried catfish.
For curious diners, that novelty is part of the appeal. Matcha also comes with a healthy reputation, which can make an unusual green dish seem somehow more virtuous than the original.

Nutrition experts, however, say the reality is more complicated. Matcha contains beneficial compounds, but sprinkling or mixing it into a rich dish does not magically transform everything else on the plate.

Senior lecturer Adnin Afifi Nawi sees much of the current craze as culinary experimentation shaped by social media. “If a food item goes viral because of its attractive colour or unique taste, there is nothing wrong with giving it a try,” he said.
“However, we should not immediately conclude that it is healthy simply because it contains matcha.”

That distinction matters in an era when food is often judged before the first bite. Adnin noted that visually striking dishes have become particularly attractive to younger consumers, with colour and novelty helping a creation stand out on TikTok or Instagram.
“The more unusual or extraordinary a dish is, the greater its potential to be shared and go viral,” he added.

The ingredient’s global popularity has also surged to the point where demand has at times outpaced supply from traditional producers in Japan. But popularity, of course, is not the same thing as nutritional value.
What matcha actually offers

Dr Norsham Juliana Nordin, an expert in chronophysiology and chrononutrition, said matcha does have a legitimate nutritional basis. It contains polyphenols, particularly catechins such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) as well as L-theanine and caffeine.
These compounds have been studied for their antioxidant properties and potential roles in supporting metabolism, cardiovascular health and inflammation control.
But that does not mean every matcha-flavoured creation deserves a health-food label.
“When matcha is added to nasi lemak, burgers, noodles, traditional cakes or desserts, we cannot automatically assume that the entire dish has become a ‘health food’,” Juliana said.

“The nutritional value is still determined by the overall dish. If only a small amount of matcha is added while the food remains high in calories, sugar, saturated fat or sodium, the overall nutritional impact does not change dramatically.”
In other words, the green ingredient matters less than everything surrounding it: portion size, cooking method, sugar, fat, salt, and how often the food is eaten.

That becomes especially relevant with dishes such as matcha nasi lemak. Adding matcha to the rice may contribute some polyphenols while changing its colour and flavour, but it does not cancel out the coconut milk, sambal, fried accompaniments or sodium.

A more meaningful way to make the dish nutritionally balanced would be to moderate portions and the amount of coconut milk, oil and salt, while adding vegetables and choosing less oily accompaniments.

The same logic applies to matcha-marinated catfish. The tea powder may add flavour, colour and phenolic compounds, but a fish coated in matcha and then deep-fried in plenty of oil is still shaped nutritionally by the frying process.

“The greater difference to health usually comes from how the fish is cooked,” Juliana noted. Grilling, baking or roasting with controlled amounts of oil and salt generally has a stronger impact on the overall nutritional profile than simply adding matcha.
Cooking can also reduce some of matcha’s beneficial compounds. Notably, catechins are sensitive to heat, although they are not necessarily destroyed completely.
One study on matcha-enriched biscuits found that baking reduced total catechin content by about 19%, while other research suggests some catechins survive baking better than others.
“The higher the temperature and the longer the exposure, the greater the likelihood of changes occurring,” Juliana said.
That makes a matcha latte, chilled dessert and deep-fried matcha dish very different propositions, even if they all carry the same green label.
More is not always better
The healthy image surrounding matcha can create another problem: people may assume they can consume more of something simply because matcha is involved.

A sugary matcha drink is still sugary, while a matcha cake remains dessert. Several strong matcha drinks a day, on top of matcha snacks and sweets, can also add considerably more caffeine than some people realise.

Juliana said caffeine-sensitive individuals may experience headaches, palpitations, restlessness or sleep problems. Timing matters, too: a matcha drink in the morning is not likely to affect sleep in the same way as a heavily caffeinated one late at night.

Very high doses of concentrated green tea extracts raise separate concerns. She noted that the European Food Safety Authority has linked daily intakes of 800mg or more of EGCG from supplements with increased liver enzyme levels, although ordinary food and drinks are different from highly concentrated extracts.

The simpler rule, she concluded, is not to mistake colour for health. “There is nothing wrong with enjoying matcha, but do not eat with your eyes alone. Health cannot be judged by colour or a single ingredient.”
08e5b7e60ae055dd: MEXICO CITY: The celebrations will run long and hard in the Mercedes camp after the crowning of 20-year-old Kimi Antonelli as the youngest ever world champion, but there is one man for whom the Italian's joy will be tinged with regret.
After all, this season was supposed to be all about George Russell.
After dominating early season testing, Russell went into the campaign as universal favourite to take the title, the heir to Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes ready to assume his place in the pantheon.

That status was reinforced by an imposing victory in the opening race in Australia. Since then, however, that early optimism has turned to ashes as he has had to watch the young pretender steal in and claim his crown.
Russell needed to win in Mexico to have any hope of stalling the young Italian but a faltering sixth place, which included a 10-second penalty for bumping Isack Hadjar, was nowhere near good enough.
But it summed up a disappointing season of mistakes and bad luck.
"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to, in all honesty," the Englishman said before the race in Mexico.
"The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense and that's because we all care so much for what we're doing."
Russell has always been candid and he will undoubtedly think back to a perfect opening weekend in Melbourne and wonder how it all went so badly wrong.

He dominated qualifying, taking pole position with three-tenths of a second in hand over Antonelli, and followed up by winning the race with a three-second gap to his teammate with the rest flailing in his wake.
Was there a touch of complacency, however, behind his smile on the podium?
"After his performances in Australia and given the gap to the other teams, he already pictured himself as world champion. Maybe he got ahead of himself a bit too soon," a paddock insider told AFP.
Fourth in the 2025 championship with twice as many points as Antonelli, who was in his rookie F1 season, the 28-year-old Englishman cannot have foreseen such a tussle with his teammate.
Not that it was much of a tussle: Antonelli has proved stronger in his head and on the track all season.
'Struggling'
Things quickly went off the rails for Russell.
Despite a pole position and a sprint win at the second event in China, Russell then watched, powerless, as Antonelli delivered a masterclass to claim his first ever grand prix win.
It was the first of five consecutive wins for the Italian which left his teammate reeling.
After his victory in early June in Monaco, the sixth round of the season, Antonelli already held a 68-point lead over a disheartened Russell, who was running third behind Hamilton.
Hit with two penalties in Monaco, where he dropped from third to 12th place right at the end of the race, the Englishman fumed.
"I'm beyond frustrated and I'm struggling to understand how this season is unfolding," he said.
Russell has certainly had his share of misfortune this season, as he was forced to retire in Canada and Malaysia due to technical problems, and in Belgium after being hit by Hamilton.
Antonelli, by contrast, has on several occasions benefited from safety car interventions, as in his victory in Madrid.

But Russell seemed to give in far too early. After his retirement at Spa, he said he felt "numbed by disappointment", and as early as the summer break he considered the gap to his teammate almost impossible to close.

There were glimmers of the old Russell as he pulled out superb drives to win in Austria and Azerbaijan but by then it was all but over with the gap between the two drivers sharply illustrated by the Italian GP at Monza.
Russell qualified second while Antonelli was forced to begin in 19th. The race was Russell's to lose, which he did.
He finished second, nearly four seconds behind the winner, Antonelli, who had picked his way through the field in one of the all-time great drives.
In Austin last week, before the US Grand Prix, a disarmingly straight Russell said what everyone has been thinking: "I haven't been up to the task."
No one can argue with that but ahead of Mexico, Russell hinted that his best is yet to come.
"I remind myself that I'm 28 and I see Lewis (Hamilton) still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando (Alonso) at 45," he said.
"And you know Lewis won the majority of his titles in his thirties so this year is absolutely not going to define my career as a whole.
"It's not going to break me. If anything, it's going to make me stronger."
5b5ab5941c08e86f: KYIV: The longest truce of the Ukraine war, limited to the eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday after Russia refused the offer of an extension, Ukrainian officials said.

The rare pause in fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and which began early Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as the war grinds through its fifth year.
Neither side reported violations after the truce began, in what one Ukrainian lawmaker described as the "biggest de-escalation since 2022."
"The ceasefire, which was in effect from Oct 27 to Nov 1, has ended," said Ukraine's Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets.
He called the temporary truce "an important step in our joint humanitarian efforts" with Russia.
US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume this month, having been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February.
- 'FRESH AIR' FOR KHERSON RESIDENTS -

The conflict, sparked by Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion, has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead, and forced millions to flee their homes.
AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a "breath of fresh air."
"We have to use this time to get things done," said Volodymyr Omeltchenko, a 38-year-old gardener. "We're pruning the rose bushes for winter."
Pope Leo, who had pressed Russia for a truce in Oleshky, said he hoped the temporary pause would "strengthen the desire for dialogue and lead to new concrete peace initiatives."
A Ukrainian military officer, speaking on condition of anonymity, expressed concern that the fighting would be "worse than before" when it resumed.

Russian forces, positioned on the other side of the Dnipro river, had taken advantage of the calm of the past few days to amass new troops, transport ammunition stocks, and collect intelligence on Ukrainian positions using surveillance drones, the officer said.
Kherson regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin warned local people to be particularly vigilant when the ceasefire ended and to "respond immediately to warnings about Russian attacks."

Later Sunday, Ukraine's air force and anti-disinformation centre said they suspected the country's air raid alert system had been hacked, after false alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the application.
"The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference," the force said in a message. "There is no radiation threat."
- REFINERY REPORTEDLY HIT -
Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes elsewhere on Sunday.
Russia said early Sunday that a drone had struck an "industrial enterprise" east of Moscow overnight.
Ukrainian media reported that Kyiv had attacked the Kstovo oil refinery, calling it "one of Russia's largest oil refineries, producing fuel and lubricants."
Kyiv has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites, in what it says is fair retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
US President Donald Trump had been pressing Kyiv to stop such attacks, blaming them for rising diesel costs that analysts attribute to the Iran war.
Ukraine's energy ministry reported fresh power outages across the country Sunday, including in Kyiv, following Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
Ukrainian strikes killed five people in Russian-occupied Ukraine between late Saturday and Sunday afternoon, Russian-installed authorities said.
Both Russia and Ukraine deny targeting civilians.

Russia now occupies around a fifth of its neighbour: the Crimean peninsula, which it annexed in 2014, most of the eastern regions of Donetsk and Lugansk – collectively referred to as the Donbas – and large parts of the southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions.--AFP

24db15e217bfc3be: UNITED NATIONS: The 35-year-old UN peacekeeping mission in the Western Sahara region will come to an end after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate, the UN chief said on Sunday.
Morocco, which claims the Western Sahara as its own, welcomed the decision, while its opponents in the Algeria-backed Polisario Front expressed concern.
The Polisario Front has been seeking an independent state in Western Sahara since former colonial power Spain left in 1976.
A peacekeeping mission, known as Minurso, has been in place there since a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991.
Nov 1 would mark the start of the “liquidation phase” of the mission, with assets transported back to troop-contributing countries, UN chief Antonio Guterres said in a statement.

The end of the peacekeeping mission comes a year after the UN Security Council adopted a US-drafted resolution that accepted Rabat's plan to give the territory autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty as the "most feasible" solution to the conflict.

Russia, which abstained in last year's vote, this year vetoed another US-backed resolution that would have cemented the UN's preference for the Moroccan plan while scaling back the peacekeeping force.
The Security Council then defeated a competing Russian resolution, leaving the mission to expire without a new mandate.
Besides monitoring the ceasefire, Minurso was tasked with organising a referendum that has never taken place due to disagreements over voter eligibility.
Morocco's foreign minister Nasser Bourita told state media that the mission's reference to a referendum -- the “R” in its name -- was an "anachronism".
Rabat had been informed that Russia was going to block the US-drafted resolution, but saw it as "an opportunity to review certain rules of the game", he said.
Morocco's royal palace had said the non-renewal of the mission was a "significant development" towards withdrawing the Western Sahara issue from consideration by the Security Council.
Algeria's foreign ministry on Saturday expressed "deep regret" over the non-renewal, blaming the "excessive bias" of the US towards Morocco's position.
The Polisario said in a statement it was "concerned at the deadlock in the Security Council meeting".
8d8227e52875b593: In 1968, Stanford biologist Paul Ehrlich opened his book The Population Bomb with a sentence that still makes me wince: "The battle to feed all of humanity is over." In the 1970s, he predicted, "hundreds of millions of people will starve to death", no matter what crash programmes we launched.

Instead came the Green Revolution, and between 1960 and 2005 the yields of major cereal crops more than doubled while real food prices fell by over 50%. Yet when a New York Times documentary series asked him about the book in 2015, Ehrlich, who died in March at 93, replied: "My language would be even more apocalyptic today."

I can't help but feel we are watching the same film again, except that this time the bomb is AI. And here's the kicker: the people who understand it best are far less frightened of it than the rest of us.

When the Pew Research Center surveyed Americans in 2024, 51% said they were more concerned than excited about AI, against a mere 15% of the 1,013 AI experts it polled. More than half of those experts, 56%, expected AI to have a positive impact on the United States over the next 20 years, compared with just 17% of the public.

Malaysians, refreshingly, haven't quite caught the bug. In market research firm Ipsos' 2025 survey of 30 countries, 77% of us said AI excites us, the third highest of the lot, though 55% admitted it also makes us nervous.

Now, I'm no doe-eyed optimist. In July, during an internal hacking test, roughly 700 of OpenAI's AI agents found exposed login credentials and broke into the servers of Hugging Face, an outside AI hosting company, and investigators found that the agents knew "this activity was out of scope and unethical", but joined in anyway.

Closer to home, by August 2024 the police's Commercial Crime Investigation Department was already probing 454 scams believed to involve deepfakes, AI-generated fake voices and videos, with RM2.72 million lost. And 63% of Malaysians worry that AI could take their job within the next three to five years.
These are grave dangers, which is exactly why we must build the brakes as we go. But a danger is not a destiny, and the odds, according to the researchers building this technology, are in our favour.

In a survey conducted in late 2023, 2,778 researchers who had published at top AI conferences and journals put the median chance of an extremely bad outcome, such as human extinction, at 5%. That's not nothing, but 68.3% of them said good outcomes were more likely than bad ones.
So what does the good outcome look like? We don't have to imagine it, because much of it is already here:
● Google DeepMind's AlphaFold mapped over 200 million protein shapes, earning its creators a Nobel Prize;
● AI-assisted screening of Swedish women caught 29% more breast cancers, with 44% less radiologist work;
● An AI at University of California San Diego cut hospital sepsis deaths by 17%; and
● A generative AI assistant lifted customer support productivity by 14%, and that of novice workers by 34%

That last point matters to anyone worried about their job, because the tool helped the least experienced workers the most, narrowing the gap between the rookie and the veteran rather than widening it. Just this week, Microsoft said its diagnostic AI correctly diagnosed 83% of complex medical cases against 36% for generalist doctors in a study published in the journal Science, though it has yet to be tested against specialists or on real patients.

And it's already at work in our own public health system. Dr Mata, an AI developed by the Ministry of Health with private firm Qmed Asia, screens diabetics for retinopathy, a leading cause of preventable blindness here, in about 30 seconds, in a country where 15.6% of adults have type 2 diabetes.

Meanwhile, seven government clinics, from Kajang in Selangor to Kok Lanas in Kelantan, were picked last year to pilot AI-assisted chest X-rays designed to catch lung disease earlier, at a one-off software cost of about RM10,000 per clinic.

Where does it go from here? Demis Hassabis, the Nobel laureate who runs Google DeepMind, told CBS's 60 Minutes last year that ending all disease is "within reach. Maybe within the next decade or so, I don't see why not", before asking in the same interview: "Can we make sure that we can keep control of the systems?"
That is precisely the right posture, eyes wide open to the risks but feet firmly moving towards the reward. Fear has its uses, but it makes a terrible driver.

So by all means build the brakes, fund the police's deepfake hunters and retrain the workers whose jobs will change. But the next time someone tells you the battle for humanity's future is already lost, remember the global famine that never came, and the AI our own health ministry helped build that can now screen a diabetic's eyes in 30 seconds.

153960d3fc572c32: MEXICO CITY: McLaren's outgoing Formula One world champion Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has made winning this year's title look easy and deserves far more credit for his achievement.
Mercedes driver Antonelli became the sport's youngest champion on Sunday, in only his second season, with the 20-year-old also Italy's first in 73 years.
"He's done an insane job," said Norris ahead of the race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.
"I feel like people are somehow not giving him enough credit for what he's achieved this year.
"He's beaten a teammate (George Russell) that's been in the sport four or five times longer than him, who's also very good, and took the battle to Lewis (Hamilton)."
Antonelli, third on Sunday after starting fourth, went into the Mexico City weekend 123 points clear of Russell and 124 ahead of Ferrari's seven-time champion Hamilton.
That meant the winner of nine races so far, one more than pre-season favourite Russell has managed in his career, needed only to score two points even if either of his remaining rivals won the race.
"They (critics) say, 'Oh, he's not had much competition' and everything," continued Norris. "But that's because he just slapped his competition.
"I think he's made it look an easy year, if you can make anything look easy nowadays. I think he's done an unbelievable job. Like incredible, incredible job."

Norris won the title last year by two points from Red Bull's four-time world champion Max Verstappen, who made an amazing comeback after a season that had looked early on like being in the bag for McLaren's Oscar Piastri.
The Briton was already mathematically out of contention before the Mexico weekend and said he had realised his hopes of retaining the title had gone long before that.
Antonelli's wins include Monaco, Monza and Spa and he has smashed records along the way in a run that included five wins in a row.
Russell has won three races and been inconsistent in his form, on top one weekend and off form the next, and found it harder to adapt to the new cars and rules.
"The truth is he's been at a higher level than me this year," he said earlier in the week.--REUTERS

9ba3a6f451e7bcfc: KUALA LUMPUR: For businessman and philanthropist R Rajendran, helping disadvantaged youths is more than providing financial assistance. It is about giving those who have fallen through the cracks of the education system a chance to rebuild their lives.

That is the aim of the RM7.2 million contribution to MySkills Foundation from Amalan Setar (M) Sdn Bhd, where Rajendran serves as managing director. The foundation provides vocational training and personal development programmes for school dropouts and at-risk youths.

"Many charities provide financial assistance to students in need, but MySkills is different. It removes school dropouts from the negative environment they are in and gives them the opportunity to flourish in a new environment. That is what makes this organisation special,” he said at Amalan Setar's annual dinner.
Rajendran has previously donated RM400,000 to MySkills for the construction of its male hostel, named Bala's Hall of Residence after his brother.
MySkills, established in 2010, initially operated out of a rented shoplot in Puchong before moving to Port Klang and eventually establishing its permanent campus in Kalumpang in 2018.
The latest contribution will bring the foundation's endowment fund to RM15 million, RM5 million short of its RM20 million target for next year.
MySkills Foundation CEO G Devasharma said the endowment fund was crucial to ensuring the organisation could continue supporting vulnerable youths without relying entirely on donations and grants.

The foundation, which has operated for 16 years, spends nearly RM4 million annually, while a RM20 million endowment fund is expected to generate between RM1 million and RM1.5 million in yearly investment income.
Devasharma said the foundation would continue seeking contributions even after reaching its initial fundraising target, as investment returns alone would not cover its annual expenditure.
He said a stronger endowment fund would also support plans to establish centres in other parts of the country, including Johor, Penang and the East Coast.
At its Kalumpang campus, MySkills trains 150 students annually, with the capacity to accommodate up to 250 to 300 students.
Devasharma said expanding beyond Selangor was necessary to reach more school dropouts and at-risk youths who might otherwise remain outside existing intervention programmes.
He said the foundation's approach went beyond providing vocational qualifications, with an emphasis on character development, life skills and preparing students for long-term employment.
He added that while employers were often willing to provide technical training, retaining workers was a challenge due to their attitude towards employment.

Devasharma stressed the importance of corporate participation in creating employment pathways for disadvantaged youths, saying this could help reduce reliance on migrant workers while steering vulnerable young people away from crime.

ed40bf87f685d03f: PETALING JAYA: Malaysians have become seasoned online shoppers, accustomed to flash sales, vouchers, free shipping and the endless ritual of comparing prices across platforms.

But familiarity does not necessarily translate into confidence or discernment. A recent Southeast Asian e-commerce study found that only 20% of Malaysian online shoppers met its definition of a “savvy shopper”, below the regional average of 24%.
The 2026 eCommerce Savvy Shopper Report, conducted by research firm Cube Asia, surveyed 6,000 shoppers aged 18 to 61 across Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines.

Rather than judging shoppers solely by how cheaply they bought something, the study assessed four areas: verification, value optimisation, confidence and protection, and digital fluency. To be classified as "savvy", respondents had to score above the regional median in all four.
One of the clearest weaknesses among Malaysian shoppers was verification - checking product details, reviews, seller credentials and authenticity information before buying.
Notably, 17% of Malaysian respondents met the benchmark in three of the four areas, making them "somewhat savvy" - but among this group, 45% fell short specifically on verification.

In other words, many local consumers were already comparing value, using digital tools confidently and understanding buyer protection, yet were still not consistently checking whether the seller or product itself could be trusted.
That matters in an online marketplace where similar-looking products can vary sharply in quality, authenticity and after-sales support.

The finding also suggests that an appealing discount may still carry hidden costs if a shopper has not checked who is selling the item, what protection applies, or whether the product is what it claims to be.
Savvy does not necessarily mean spending less
Perhaps the most interesting finding is that the savvier shoppers were not the most frugal. In Malaysia, those classified as "savvy" reported spending 36% more each month than general shoppers.
They also appeared more willing to pay for reassurance: 39% said they would spend more for stronger purchase protection, compared with 24% of general shoppers.
Some 43% of savvy shoppers also directed most of their spending towards marketplace “Mall” sections, where official brands and verified sellers are typically concentrated.

The implication is that confidence may matter as much as price. Shoppers who take the time to check sellers, return policies and authenticity signals may actually become more comfortable spending once they feel the risks have been reduced.
Cube Asia describes that extra effort as a kind of “confidence tax” - the additional work consumers perform before feeling certain enough to buy.

There is an obvious caveat. The research was commissioned by Lazada, which has a commercial interest in strengthening trust in online marketplaces, while the “savvy shopper” benchmarks were created specifically for this study rather than representing a universally accepted measure of consumer sophistication.
Its findings are, therefore, best read as a snapshot of certain shopping behaviours rather than an indisputable verdict that four out of five Malaysians simply do not know how to shop online.
Still, the distinction it draws is useful. Online shopping has matured well beyond the question of who can find the lowest price.

For consumers navigating an increasingly crowded digital marketplace, knowing what they are buying, who they are buying from and what happens if something goes wrong may be becoming just as important as the discount flashing on the screen.

db9b6a0dfb683fcf: GENEVA: More than 300,000 people have fled their homes in western Yemen because of intensifying fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces, the UN said on Sunday.
Almost all were displaced in the last two months, and they "urgently need shelter, food, clean water and health care", the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said in a statement.

4b4cd84e67e3a45c: PARIS: When the season started few gave thought to the possibility that Kimi Antonelli, in just his second season behind the wheel of the Mercedes in Formula One, would emerge as the youngest world champion in the 76-year history of the sport.
AFP Sport picks out six races that defined the 20-year-old's rise to the top step of the podium.
March 15: China
After following teammate George Russell over the finish line in the season-opener in Australia, Antonelli turned some heads in the next race in Shanghai.
Not only did he become the youngest driver ever to take pole position but Antonelli, still only 19, went on to win his first grand prix, becoming the second youngest F1 winner behind Max Verstappen.
Russell won the sprint and came second in the main race but can have had no inkling that this was to be the pattern for most of the season.
May 24: Canada
Antonelli continued his form and went to Montreal on the back of three successive wins while Russell, who was plagued with poor luck all season, had failed to make the podium since China.
The Englishman, however, appeared to rediscover his mojo on the street circuit, winning the sprint and taking pole position.

The race, however, again belonged to Antonelli who made it four wins on the bounce as Russell was forced to retire on lap 30 due to a battery/power unit failure, costing him a potential 18 points and widening the gap.
June 7: Monaco

Two weeks later, the Italian again started from pole to make it five wins from five with a first victory on the tight, legendary Monaco street circuit. Again, however, he benefited from his teammate's misfortune late in the race.
After being penalised for speeding in the pit lane, Russell suffered further when the Mercedes mechanics started working on his car before the penalty time elapsed.
Russell dropped from third to finish out of the points in 12th. After six races, Antonelli led Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Russell by 66 and 68 points respectively.
September 6: Italy
After winning five of the first six races, Antonelli suffered a mini-slump, winning just one (Belgium) of the next six.
Russell was trying to fight back but Antonelli's performance in front of his home crowd in Monza all but sealed the title as he produced one of the all-time great performances on a race track.

While Russell started on pole, Antonelli, in his first race as a 20-year-old, was forced to start from 19th on the grid due to an engine penalty. He then proceeded to pick his way through the field, past Russell, to become the first Italian to win the race since Ludovico Scarfiotti 60 years earlier.
Russell, eight years his senior, finished second but Antonelli's masterly performance left no one in doubt as to who was now the senior partner.
September 26: Azerbaijan
Another street circuit in Baku and this time Antonelli made a rare error when he pranged his car into a wall during qualifying.
It meant starting down in 16th while Russell, with almost the last throw of his dice, drove superbly to take pole.
The Englishman this time made no mistakes and took a commanding chequered flag but his hopes of biting into Antonelli's sizeable lead were lessened by another mature drive from the Italian.
He didn't make it on to the podium this time but worked his way up to fifth to puncture Russell's optimism and close in on the title.
October 4: Malaysia
The final nail came at the Bahrain GP which had been relocated to Malaysia because of the conflict in the Middle East.
Antonelli finished second behind a resurgent Verstappen this time but stretched his lead after Russell, who was running third at the time, was forced to retire just a few laps from the finish.
That took his lead in the championship to 84 points, effectively ending Russell's bid to challenge him and signalling a new era in Formula One.
98c8234119275043: Linus Torvalds has posted the first release candidate for version 7.4 of the Linux kernel and offered his opinion that the project has found a “much healthier model” for using AI.

“This is a *BIG* merge window,” he wrote in his weekly state of the kernel update, as it contains almost 20,000 commits compared to the usual ~15,000 that developers submit for a new cut of the kernel.

“I think the reason is the by now obvious one, but I'm actually taking it as a good sign: I'm *much* happier with the flood of AI triggered work going into the merge window than it showing up mainly as extra fixes during the -rc period.”

He therefore hopes that the unusually large number of commits “is a sign that the AI fixes are becoming more part of the ‘normal development’ than a flood of fixes that go into the whole stabilization phase.”

“I think that's a much healthier model,” he added, before hedging with the observation that “people are expecting 7.4 to be the next LTS [long-term support] release, which is another independent reason why some releases tend larger than others.”
“So it may not *just* be the flood of AI patches.”

Torvalds also seems not to be completely convinced that all AI submissions are entirely helpful, by describing this release as “Large, and full of fixes for issues found by AI (and more and more the patches have been suggested by AI too, although they often get rewritten).”
AMD GPU register offsets and bit masks make up a third of the changes this time around.
“We've been here before, and I'm sure we'll see it many times again in the future,” Torvalds wrote. “Just ignore the noise.”

The kernel-watchers at Phoronix rate the major inclusions in Linux 7.4 as improved support for processors from AMD, Apple, and Google. Other additions include some handy tweaks to improve security for virtual machines, support for the Raspberry Pi 10-inch monitor and more work to get Linux running happily on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 SoC for PCs. ®
584ca80c189f7c87: KUALA LUMPUR: Nearly 100 employees of Media Mulia Sdn Bhd, the publisher of Utusan Malaysia and Kosmo!, will be placed on paid leave as the company reviews its business model amid changes in the media landscape.

73cca6612605a5da: LIVERPOOL: Arsenal moved top of the Premier League with a statement 1-0 win at Liverpool as Manchester United plunged further into crisis with a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.
Brighton could prove to be Arsenal's biggest challenge to retaining their title after the Seagulls inflicted a second consecutive defeat on Manchester City.
AFP Sport looks at three talking points from the weekend's action:
Arsenal show grit of champions
There are few feats Mikel Arteta has not achieved since taking charge of Arsenal seven years ago but a Premier League win at Anfield had eluded him until Sunday.
Arteta got the response he desired to an embarrassing League Cup exit to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday as Kai Havertz gave the Gunners an early lead.
Thereafter, though, Arsenal needed to rely on their renowned defensive resilience.
Liverpool were made to pay for not taking their chances in a dominant spell before half-time, but the Reds were completely snuffed out in the second period once Arteta restored order at the break.

Arsenal's three-point lead at the top is even more comfortable in the context that City are likely to face a huge points deduction unless they overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules.
Could Man Utd really be relegated?
The last time United were in the relegation zone after August was 40 years ago when Ron Atkinson’s dismissal paved the way for the arrival of Alex Ferguson and a golden era of success.
That may prove the only crumb of comfort for United fans now bunkering down for the potential of a relegation battle over a long winter.
Defeats for Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace ensured the Red Devils remain just outside the bottom three on goal difference.
But United's downward spiral shows no sign of abating.
Michael Carrick was given a stay of execution for Saturday's trip to Stamford Bridge but was left with his head in his hands after a second-half implosion from the visitors.
United had enjoyed the better chances of a goalless first half.
Any sense of positivity was quickly erased when Morgan Rogers was allowed to rampage unchallenged through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring.
A moment of madness from Lisandro Martinez then did his under-fire manager no favours.
The Argentine was booked for two fouls, committed 83 seconds apart, to leave United down to 10 men and concede a penalty, which Cole Palmer converted.
A nine-game winless run is United's longest without victory for 38 years.
The realistic prospect of a club that should post revenues this season in excess of £700 million being relegated remains remote.
However, the fast start of all three promoted clubs, who all sit above Carrick's men in the table, means it cannot be easily dismissed.
Brighton dare to dream
Brighton are also dreaming of upsetting the odds but for all the right reasons.
The Seagulls have never won a major trophy but have proven they can handle the Premier League's best.
Fabian Hurzeler's men thrashed Arsenal 3-0 in September and beat City away for the first time in the club's history on Saturday.
The Premier League's top scorers have also now kept six clean sheets in nine games.
"There’s an old phrase - defence wins you battles and wins you championships," said Hurzeler.
"I said before the game it's about belief, it's about having the confidence to come here and win this game."
Brighton sit third but belief is growing they could do the impossible and emulate Leicester's shock title triumph a decade ago.
